Vǫlsungakviða in forna 9 (= Helgakviða Hundingsbana II 9; FJ 1926)

notes: Candidate from the Phase 8c reader study (docs/research/8c-results.md): an addition to a known formula, not a new formula, and unconfirmed by an expert. Known: only the compound 'raw-eater' (Gk ὠμηστής = Ved. āmā́d-, West 2007 ch. 2 p. 80 with n. 16) and the word equations. The candidate is the free clause *h₂eh₃mó- + *kréwh₂s + *h₁ed-. Greek has it in one clause: Il. 22.347 ὤμ̓ … κρέα ἔδμεναι, Achilles wishing to eat Hector's flesh raw (checked in AGDT). There ὠμά agrees with κρέα but is predicative ('eat the flesh raw'). Vedic has it split: in AVŚ 8.6.23 (DCS sentence 'AVŚ, 8, 6.s48', stanza counter 23; checked) ya āmaṃ māṃsam adanti pauruṣeyaṃ ca ye kraviḥ, demons 'who eat raw meat, and who [eat] human gore'. So āmám qualifies māṃsám (not in the line) and kravíḥ is the second object of the same verb. The exact NP āmá- + kravís- stands in RV 1.162.10b āmásya kravíṣaḥ ('the smell of the raw flesh'; genitive, no verb; checked in VedaWeb). Old Norse (checked in FJ 1926) keeps eta and has hrátt, a *krewh₂- derivative 'raw' in place of *h₂eh₃mó-; the noun is renewed (kjöt). It counts for the verb only. Morphology: the athematic root present *h₁éd-/h₁d- of Ved. adánti (3pl; the lemma is cited as atti, the Sanskrit citation form of that present, so the check can find it) and of the Homeric athematic infinitive ἔδμεναι. 3pl and singular kréwh₂s follow the AV; Greek has the plural κρέα. The lexicon glosses kréwh₂s 'blood', but its reflexes here mean raw flesh or gore (kravís-), meat (κρέας) and gore (Lat. cruor); hence 'raw flesh'. Support only: the raw-eater compounds (Il. 11.454 ὠμησταί tearing corpses; RV 10.87.7d āmā́daḥ … adantu) and Od. 9.297 κρέ̓ ἔδων of the Cyclops (no 'raw'). Generic risk is real (three basic words), but the contexts agree: savage or demonic eating of human flesh.

notes: Candidate from the Phase 8c reader study (docs/research/8c-results.md): an addition to a known formula, not a new formula, and unconfirmed by an expert. Known: the word equations amŕ̥ta- = ἄμβροτος and vas- = ἕννυμι. West 2007 ch. 3 n. 126 discusses ἄμβροτα εἵματα of Sarpedon's corpse (Il. 16.680), and ch. 2 has *wes- with other coverings ('clothed in a cloud', nábho vásānaḥ ~ νεφέλην ἕσσαντο). The new element is the Vedic witness. RV 6.75.18b (= AVŚ 7.118.1, both checked) sómas tvā rā́jāmŕ̥tenā́nu vastām: 'let King Soma clothe you with the immortal', said over the warrior's armour. AVŚ 9.1.1 (DCS sentence s2, stanza counter 1; checked) has amṛ́taṃ vásānām, 'wearing the immortal'. The Greek is the stock line περὶ δ̓ ἄμβροτα εἵματα ἕσσε(ν), all checked: Il. 16.670 (imperative, Zeus to Apollo; AGDT mislemmatizes ἕσσον as ἵζω), Il. 16.680, Od. 24.59, and Hymn. Hom. 6.6 in glaux. Drift: Greek puts ἄμβροτος on the garment noun εἵματα (*wésmn̥, Greek only), while Vedic uses the substantivized neuter amŕ̥tam as the covering. The line follows the Vedic instrumental. Greek has the instrumental of a derivative beside it in the same lines: χρῖσε … ἀμβροσίῃ, 'anointed with ambrosia'. The verb is shared at root level only: Vedic has the root present (vastām, 3sg middle imperative used transitively), Greek the s-aorist (ἕσσον, ἕσσε). The engine's only *wes- 'clothe' lexeme is the nasal present *wes-néw- of ἕννυμι, which neither passage has. The builder's Greek 'exact' rests on the lemma ἕννυμι only. The lexicon has no root present *wés-tor (pie-lex-westi-2 is *wes- 'sell'). The imperative mood is shared (Il. 16.670, RV 6.75.18b). Person and active voice follow Il. 16.670 (2sg); the Vedic is 3sg middle. The object 'him' is interpolated: Sarpedon is implicit in the Greek, and the Vedic has tvā 'you'. The lexeme's gloss 'dress oneself' is the middle; the active is 'clothe someone', as with ἕννυμι.

West 2007 ch. 2 p. 84: Vedic svādór … mádhvaḥ 'of the sweet mead' = Homeric μέθυ ἡδύ, with μέθυ shifted to 'wine' (also Schmitt 1967 §529). The NP *swéh₂dus médʰu is the formula. RV 1.84.10a-b svādór itthā́ viṣūváto mádhvaḥ pibanti, 'they drink of the sweet mead' (checked in VedaWeb). The Greek μέθυ ἡδύ recurs as a line-end formula (nine times in the Odyssey: Od. 9.162, 10.184, 17.533 and others; checked in AGDT). The Old English witness swētne medo, 'the sweet mead' repaid by retainers (Finnsburh 39, checked in the Gutenberg Beowulf appendix), is the 8c Stage A addition (8c-results.md: West and Schmitt cite Vedic and Greek only). OE swēte continues the u-stem *swōtu- moved into the ja-stems, so the builder's 'exact' for it is generous: formation level. The line is the bare noun phrase, realized as an np utterance (no verb and no copula: David's review, the earlier 'There is sweet mead' with an interpolated existential h₁ésti is withdrawn), attributive as in all three branches, with the adjective first as in Vedic and Old English (Greek has the noun first, μέθυ ἡδύ). The frames differ and none is shared: Vedic pibanti 'drink' (the reduplicated present *pí-ph₃-e-, which the lexicon cannot inflect), Greek δαινύμενοι 'feasting' (Od. 9.162) and ἔδουσιν 'eat' (Od. 17.533), OE forgyldan 'repay'. The cases differ too: Vedic partitive genitive, Greek and OE accusative; the nominative is the citation case of the bare NP and is interpolated. RV 8.49.4b mádhvaḥ svā́diṣṭham has the superlative (root level) and is not cited. Generic risk: a honey drink is naturally sweet, but the pairing is a fixed formula in Greek and is claimed as inherited by West. Old English swētne medo (Finnsburh 39) is Ettmüller's emendation; the manuscript reads hwitne 'white' (tier2 review r3): kept as support only.

notes: Phase 8c Stage A claim C048 (accepted; 8c-results.md: 'partly known', not one of the three final candidates). West 2007 ch. 3 p. 158 with n. 127 has only the motif: the gods' horses are immortal, Greek and Iranian. Durante 1976, which we do not hold, may already have the lexical match. Unconfirmed by an expert. AVŚ 13.1.24 (DCS sentence s47, stanza counter 24; checked): sū́ryasyā́śvā hárayaḥ ketumántaḥ sádā vahanty amṛ́tāḥ sukháṃ rátham, 'the Sun's bay horses always draw, immortal, the easy-running chariot'. Il. 16.380-381 = 16.866-867 (checked in AGDT): ὠκέες ἵπποι | ἄμβροτοι, οὓς Πηλῆϊ θεοὶ δόσαν, Achilles' god-given horses. In both, n̥mr̥tó- stands in apposition to the plural horse noun ('the horses, immortal …'). The line is the apposition itself, realized as an np utterance with n̥mr̥tós as APPOS after the plural horse noun, as both passages have it (David's review: the earlier predicate 'The horses are immortal' with an interpolated copula h₁sénti is withdrawn). No verb and no copula; the frames differ (Vedic vahanti 'draw', Greek the relative clause οὓς … δόσαν), the nominative plural is the case of both passages. Generic risk is medium: 'immortal' is freely applied to divine things in both traditions. The line's 'swift' (ὠκέες) belongs to the separate swift-horses formula (divine-twins-004) and is not used. Hymn. Hom. 2.375-376 (renewed ἀθανάτους) is not cited.

Round 3 draft (docs/audits/tier2-round3-drafts.md), from the formula witness scan (docs/research/formula-witness-scan.md); not yet reviewed. West 2007 ch. 12 'horses and men' (west_ch12_f17). This line takes the *h₂nḗr branch pair; the *wiHrós pair is epic-diction-006. Greek: the stock coordination ἵπποι τε καὶ ἄνδρες, checked in AGDT at Il. 23.242 (nominative) and Il. 10.338 (genitive ἵππων τε καὶ ἀνδρῶν); also Il. 8.214, 17.740, 21.16 (genitive), 2.554, 11.497, 16.167 (accusative). Vedic RV 10.68.12cd (checked in VedaWeb): Br̥haspati gives vigour 'with cows, with horses, with heroes, with men' (góbhiḥ … áśvaiḥ … vīrébhiḥ … nŕ̥bhiḥ), instrumental plurals in an anaphoric list, so the Vedic is a list, not a two-member coordination. Support RV 7.41.3cd (= AVŚ 3.16.3; the scan's 'AVŚ, 3, 16.s6' is DCS sentence 6, i.e. stanza 3): góbhir áśvaiḥ in one pāda, nŕ̥bhiḥ in the next. Interpolated: the nominative (Greek Il. 23.242; Vedic has the instrumental) and the conjunction: the engine's X Y-kʷe, where Greek has X τε καὶ Y (τε < *-kʷe after the first member) and Vedic has none. Generic risk: horses and men is a natural pair in any war narrative; West counts it as inherited because of the Celtic witness (epic-diction-006).

Ce.locus: Síaburcharpat Con Culainn (CELT G301008, ed. p. 49 l. 19)
Síaburcharpat Con Culainn (CELT G301008, ed. p. 49 l. 19)

notes: Round 3 draft (docs/audits/tier2-round3-drafts.md), from the formula witness scan (docs/research/formula-witness-scan.md); not yet reviewed. West 2007 ch. 12 'horses and men' (west_ch12_f17), the *wiHrós branch pair. Old Irish: Síaburcharpat Con Culainn, Benén's answer bátar anála fer ⁊ ech 'it was the breath of men and horses' (CELT G301008, edition p. 49 l. 19; the same text in Lebor na hUidre, CELT G301900, LU l. 9246; both read in the CELT XML). Genitive plural fer ⁊ ech, men first. The scan's third Irish witness, Fingal Rónáin (G302011) ind ḟir, ind óïc, ind eich, is a three-member list and is not used. Vedic RV 9.96.11d vīrébhir áśvair maghávā bhavā naḥ 'be bountiful to us with men and horses' (instrumental, men first; checked in VedaWeb). AVŚ 12.1.25 yó aśveṣu vīreṣu (locative, horses first; DCS chapter 'AVŚ, 12, 1', stanza counter 25; the scan's 'AVŚ, 12, 1.s53' is the DCS sentence index, not the stanza). Avestan Rām Yašt (Yt. 15) has the same locative pair aspaēšu vīraēšu (CAB YtWay12.12a; the CAB id is given because the CAB karde numbering does not map one to one onto Geldner's stanzas); also Yt. 10 aspaēca paiti vīraēca (CAB YtMihr26.4f). Renewal: Greek replaced *wiHrós by ἀνήρ (Il. 20.157 ἀνδρῶν ἠδ’ ἵππων, men first, genitive, cited as support for the order and case only). Case and order follow Old Irish (genitive, men first), which RV 9.96.11d shares in order. Interpolated: the conjunction -kʷe (OIr ⁊, Vedic none).

Round 3 draft (docs/audits/tier2-round3-drafts.md), from the formula witness scan (docs/research/formula-witness-scan.md); not yet reviewed. West 2007 ch. 2 (west_ch02_f38; Schulze's ἱερὸν μένος ~ iṣiréṇa mánasā). Greek ἱερὸν μένος + genitive of a name, 'the strong might of X': Od. 7.167 and 8.2 (Alcinous; also Od. 8.4, 8.385, 8.421, 13.20, 13.24, 18.34 Antinous), Hymn. Hom. 3.371 ἱερὸν μένος Ἠελίοιο (GLAUx 0013-003). Here ἱερός keeps its old sense 'vigorous, strong', = Ved. iṣirá-. Vedic RV 8.48.7a iṣiréṇa te mánasā sutásya bhakṣīmáhi 'may we partake of you, pressed, with vigorous mind' (checked in VedaWeb; the only RV instance of iṣirá- with mánas-). Both words are exact in both branches. Construal differs: Greek a nominative periphrasis for a person, Vedic an instrumental of manner; the line takes the Greek nominative. English follows the lexeme glosses ('strong', 'mind'); Greek μένος means 'might, fury' here.

Round 3 draft (docs/audits/tier2-round3-drafts.md), from the formula witness scan (docs/research/formula-witness-scan.md); not yet reviewed. West 2007 ch. 2 (west_ch02_f35). Greek μένος ἠΰ 'good menos', checked in AGDT/GLAUx: Il. 17.456 and 24.442 (a god breathes it into horses), also Il. 20.80, 23.524, 24.6, Od. 2.271. AGDT lemmatizes ἠΰ as ἐΰς; the citation lemma ἠΰς is the lexicon's reflex. Avestan vohu manah- 'good thought' (CAB): Y. 34.8c dūirē vohū as manō 'good thought (is) far (from them)', nominative, appellative; Y. 48.12b vohū manaŋhā 'with good thought' (instrumental). Caveat: Vohu Manah is also the name of an Aməša Spənta, and many Gathic instances sit between concept and entity; the two loci were chosen because they read as appellative. West's Vedic comparison bhadrám mánaḥ (RV 2.26.2, 10.20.1) has a non-cognate adjective and is not cited; Vedic vásu- is not found with mánas-. Both lexemes are exact in Greek and Avestan. Construal: Greek has the accusative object, Avestan nominative and instrumental; the line takes the nominative.

Round 3 draft (docs/audits/tier2-round3-drafts.md), from the formula witness scan (docs/research/formula-witness-scan.md); not yet reviewed. West 2007 ch. 2 'bold spirit' (west_ch02_f36). The head is secure: μένος = mánas- (exact in both branches). The modifier is not: Greek μένος πολυθαρσές (Il. 17.156, 19.37; also Od. 13.387; checked in AGDT/GLAUx) has the compound adjective πολυ-θαρσής (*dʰers-, s-stem θάρσος); Vedic dhr̥ṣán mánaḥ (RV 1.54.3b, 5.35.4c, also 8.62.5a; checked in VedaWeb) has dhr̥ṣát, which VedaWeb tags as a present active participle of √dhr̥ṣ-. Both share only the root *dʰers-. The lexicon's adjective *dʰr̥sús 'bold' (Gk θρασύς, Ved. dhr̥ṣṇú-) is not usable, so the line uses the active participle of the nasal present *dʰr̥snéwti (Ved. dhr̥ṣṇóti); dʰr̥snuwónt is not the formation of either passage, and the builder's 'exact' for the Vedic lemma dhr̥ṣ- reaches the nasal present through the root only. Read this as 'mind + a *dʰers- modifier', root-level. Support: Il. 5.2 μένος καὶ θάρσος (coordinated nouns, a different construction). Compounds dhr̥ṣanmanas- (RV, 2×) and θρασυμέμνων (Il. 5.639) are not equivalent: the Greek second member is μέμνων, not μένος.

english: They clothed themselves in a cloud.

plan.english: They clothed themselves in a cloud.

notes: Round 3 draft (docs/audits/tier2-round3-drafts.md), from the formula witness scan (docs/research/formula-witness-scan.md); not yet reviewed. West 2007 ch. 2 'clothed in a cloud' (west_ch02_f48), the aorist line (epic-diction-011 is the participle line). Greek (AGDT): Il. 14.350 ἐπὶ δὲ νεφέλην ἕσσαντο (Zeus and Hera), Il. 20.150 ἀμφὶ δ’ ἄρ’ ἄρρηκτον νεφέλην ὤμοισιν ἕσαντο (the gods): s-aorist middle 3pl with the cloud in the accusative. Vedic (VedaWeb): RV 5.63.6c abhrā́ vasata marútaḥ 'the Maruts clothe themselves in clouds' (accusative plural) and RV 5.85.4c sám abhréṇa vasata párvatāsaḥ 'the mountains clothe themselves with cloud' (instrumental): 3pl middle injunctive of the root present vas-. The verb is shared at root level only: Greek s-aorist (*wḗs-, exact in Greek), Vedic root present (*wés-tor). The cloud word is cognate at root level only: νεφέλη (*nebʰ-el-) against abhrá- (*n̥bʰ-ró-, = Gk ὄμβρος). The line follows the Greek formation in both slots, so the Vedic is root-level throughout. Interpolated: none beyond the pro-drop 3pl subject.

Round 3 draft (docs/audits/tier2-round3-drafts.md), from the formula witness scan (docs/research/formula-witness-scan.md); not yet reviewed. West 2007 ch. 2 'clothed in a cloud' (west_ch02_f48), the participle line. Vedic RV 9.83.5b nábho vásānaḥ pári yāsy adhvarám 'wearing cloud, you go round the sacrifice' (Soma; root-present middle participle of vas- + accusative nábhas-; checked in VedaWeb). Greek Il. 15.308 εἱμένος ὤμοιιν νεφέλην (Apollo, 'clad about his shoulders in cloud'; perfect middle participle; AGDT). The participle is the middle participle of the root present *wés-tor, the Vedic formation; Greek has the perfect participle (root level). The noun is nébʰos, the Vedic word (nábhas-, exact); Greek has νεφέλη, a derivative (*nebʰelā-), so the Greek is root level; the builder's 'exact' for νεφέλη under *nébʰos is a mapping error (νεφέλη belongs to *nebʰelos). The head 'he' (closed:demonstrative_so) is interpolated: the referent is Soma in the Veda, Apollo in Homer. Support RV 7.97.6d nábho ná rūpám … vásānāḥ (nábhas- in a simile, not the garment).

english: Willing, let him eat with the willing ones.

plan.english: Willing, let him eat with the willing ones.

notes: Round 3 draft (docs/audits/tier2-round3-drafts.md), from the formula witness scan (docs/research/formula-witness-scan.md); not yet reviewed. West 2007 ch. 2 'willing with the willing' (west_ch02_f99), a polyptoton of the participle of *weḱ- 'wish'. Vedic RV 10.15.8d uśánn uśádbhiḥ pratikāmám attu 'willing with the willing, let (Yama) eat at will' (nominative + instrumental, checked in VedaWeb); RV 1.71.1a uśatī́r uśántam (the willing wives, the willing husband). Greek (GLAUx): Aesch. PV 218 ἑκόνθ’ ἑκόντι Ζηνὶ συμπαραστατεῖν (GLAUx line attribute 220), Eur. Cycl. 258 ἑκὼν ἑκοῦσι. ἑκών (*wéḱ-ont-) and uśánt- (*uḱ-ónt-) are the same participle with different ablaut; the engine's active participle has the zero grade of the Vedic. The verb 'eat' is Vedic only (attu, *h₁ed-) and is interpolated, as are the pronoun heads of the two participles; the Greek construes the second member with a dative and a verb 'stand beside'. Archaic Greek has no instance; the Greek witnesses are tragedy (Homer has ἐθέλων ἐθέλουσαν, non-cognate, Od. 3.272).

Round 3 draft (docs/audits/tier2-round3-drafts.md), from the formula witness scan (docs/research/formula-witness-scan.md); not yet reviewed. West 2007 ch. 2 and ch. 3 'gods and mortals' (west_ch02_f64, west_ch03_f11), a polar expression. Vedic RV 1.100.15a ná yásya devā́ devátā ná mártāḥ 'whose (limit) neither the gods … nor mortals (reached)' (VedaWeb). Greek Il. 24.533 οὔ τε θεοῖσι τετιμένος οὔ τε βροτοῖσιν and Il. 15.99 οὔ τε βροτοῖσιν οὔ τε θεοῖς (AGDT): the same 'neither gods nor mortals'. Renewal: Greek replaced *deywós by θεός, so *deywós is attested in Indo-Iranian only (Ved. devá-, Av. daēuua-) and is interpolated for Greek; *mr̥tós is exact in Vedic (márta-) and Greek (βροτός). Avestan Y. 29.4b (= Y. 48.1c) daēuuāišcā maṣ̌iiāišcā 'by daēvas and men' has the double -cā (*-kʷe … -kʷe), but maṣ̌iia- is *mr̥tyo- (= Ved. mártya-), a different formation: the builder's 'exact' for maṣ̌iia- under *mr̥tós is a mapping error. Interpolated: nominative and the single -kʷe; the Vedic and Greek witnesses are negated (ná … ná, οὔ τε … οὔ τε), which the np line drops. Latin has di immortales and mortales separately; Lucr. 1.1015 and 5.1169 juxtapose divom and mortale/mortalia but not as a coordination, so no Latin witness is cited.
